D ATA  B R E A K D O W N
AEOP Social Media
Carson Guise, Marketing and Social Media Student Assistant 
January 2025 - May 2025

P R E S E N TAT I O N  O V E R V I E W
• Overview 
• Challenges
• What Worked 
• Numerical Analysis
• Concluding Thoughts

O V E R V I E W
The AEOP Social Media platforms (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and X) can 
leverage a lot of weight when it comes to reaching both the target and ideal audiences 
(potential applicants, families of the applicants, and those who have already applied / 
been involved in the program). 
The main goal of the social media platforms should be to facilitate:
• REACH
• IMPRESSIONS
• Interactions
Throughout my time here, I have found these to weigh the most crucial KPIs because 
sometimes those interested do not to follow, making these priority KPIs 
instead of follower count for example (but it still yields important)

C H A L L E N G E S  
• The main challenge that made content creation difficult was finding relevant and 
engaging content that could promote further reach. Being able to utilize the 
blogs that USAEOP publishes was great to highlight real cases of researchers 
doing applicable work, but turning those blogs into something engaging was 
sometimes challenging. 
• Another challenge was figuring out how to repurpose a post on the more 
conversational platforms (Instagram, X, and Facebook) to a more professional 
tone for LinkedIn. LinkedIn is our strongest platform so repurposing the content 
for LinkedIn was challenging, but not impossible.
• X proved to be a challenging platform in terms of engagement, 
making it almost not needed, but good to keep to give applicants 
another touchpoint to see our content off of.

W H AT  W O R K E D
• The main driver behind the social media strategy was CONSISTENCY. Having the 
consistent schedule of Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday at similar times gave 
the social media platforms structure compared to how they were before I started 
this January. 
• Using data to formulate posts, posting times, and platforms helped build off of 
small successes and turn them into bigger wins is what helped drive reach. For 
example, using the data it became obvious that LinkedIn should be a top priority 
because of it’s success in post interactions compared to the other platforms 
(ended with a 126.58% increase in post interactions - as seen later)
• Collaboration is what helped build a cohesive strategy. Once Brit 
came back, content creation became more efficient because of her 
insights. Teamwork drives marketing.

N U M E R I C A L  A N A LY S I S
This next section is to highlight how consistency and engaging content can drive up 
the overall performance and effectiveness of a good social media strategy. All of the 
data is from January 13th to May 1st.

Chart data: Impressions total 24,370, change +8,784 (+56.36%). LinkedIn 9,775, change +4,810 (+96.88%). Instagram 7,766, change +954 (+14.00%). Facebook 6,087, change +2,605 (+74.81%). Twitter/X 742, change +415 (+126.91%).

Chart data: Post interactions total 1,674, change +838 (+100.24%). LinkedIn 1,040, change +581 (+126.58%). Facebook 433, change +296 (+216.06%). Instagram 142, change -75 (-34.56%). Twitter/X 59, change +36 (+156.52%). Followers total 2,804, change +54 (+1.96%). LinkedIn 1,512, change +89 (+6.25%). Facebook 645, change 0 (0.00%). Instagram 508, change +14 (+2.83%). Twitter/X 139, change -49 (-26.06%).

Having a sustainable social media presence can ultimately drive the number of 
applcations while driving overall interest rates in AEOP. To build off that, 
consistenty and engaging content should be at the forefront of the priorities for 
the social media plan moving forward.
Having an emphasis on fellowships and internships can really hone in on 
envolvement numbers and overall interaction numbers (when posting about 
fellowships, mention pay - has lead to more engagement). 
Staying current and up-to-date on social media trends can help involvment. It is 
curical that current trends are adatpted to have better exposure. Content should

be curated to the target market in terms of copy, relevance, and 
stickiness.
